coverage.oracle: Literal code-point alphabet: empty, NUL, prefix, combining/composed forms, lone surrogate, U+10000 and two astral symbols; fixed inverse-code permutation.

65 ascending Int64 literals selected for hash collisions; numeric sorted order and first/last representative positions are independent of the hash implementation.64 present classes plus one missing colliding key.

Literal duplicate-key/raw-index and dense sorted-code answers, with unknown class -1 and destination guard words.

python_review.reason: Exercises confusion/precision/recall/f-score public encoding, explicit class subsets, Python binding seams, warning classes and unsupported label types. The new score-key suite covers only shared union/inverse ordering, not those metric outputs. Its mock binding controllers require separate review against the native callback contract; no controller was deleted to hide a failure.
Covers poisoned Python Array methods, exact container admission, huge public integers, refused user protocols and warning delivery. These cannot be replaced by raw native key records.

General labels encoder accepts floating labels and has a different native path and API. Score classification keys deliberately admit only integer/text labels. Moving its signed-zero/NaN checks onto the score-key implementation would test the wrong contract. Actual Array input, public output dtype, encoder cap, argmax and decode-gather checks remain distinct.

remaining_boundary_seams: Exact NumPy bool/integer/string normalization and custom hook refusal remain Python admission tests.
Float labels including signed zero, infinities and NaNs are refused before native score-key construction; no unsupported float key mode was invented.
Integers beyond Python's decimal-string limit are admitted through hexadecimal magnitude storage; boundary coverage remains required.
Public explicit duplicate class-list refusal is distinct from the internal index keep_last dictionary behavior.
deletions: None: no existing pure test invokes this new key-index API. Retained Python tests exercise public admission or different encoder/metric paths.
